posts.title: Balance versus what remains
posts.headline: Your bank balance is the start of the calculation, not always what remains.
posts.hypothesis: A visible balance-versus-remaining calculation will create stronger product recognition and more completed first positions than an abstract budgeting message.
posts.primaryMeasurementGoal: First-position activation rate: first_position_saved divided by qualified landing sessions attributed to ct-w01-a01.
posts.killCriteria: After at least 30 qualified visits, treat the message as weak if fewer than 5% start a preview, fewer than 3% save a first position, or repeated comments show that the balance-versus-remaining distinction is unclear.
posts.sourceOrRationale: Approved positioning, verified manual_inputs and position_calculation product facts, and the draft Journal guide why-your-bank-balance-is-not-always-what-you-can-spend.

linkedin.text:
I built ClearTill to fill the gap most banking apps miss: what is coming up.

Future bills and income shape what may remain before payday. ClearTill brings the balance, dates and costs you enter together, so your estimated daily spending amount is immediately visible.

Recurring costs can carry forward on a paid plan. Set them once instead of entering the same bill every month; just keep your balance and dates current.

That is why your bank balance is only a snapshot. It is not always the amount that may remain before payday.

Illustrative example:
Balance today: £1,250
Bills and costs still due: £1,015
Estimated amount remaining: £235

I built ClearTill to keep that distinction visible. Its output is an estimate based on the figures you enter, not financial advice or a guarantee.

Read the ClearTill Journal guide, then check your own position free:

posts.title: No bank connection
posts.headline: Know what may remain without connecting your bank.
posts.hypothesis: Explaining manual control as a deliberate no-bank-connection choice will reduce privacy objections while maintaining qualified interest in trying ClearTill.

linkedin.text:
ClearTill does not require a bank login or Open Banking connection. That is a product choice, not a claim that connected tools are unsafe.

You enter the balance, dates and costs you want included. The trade-off is straightforward: you need to keep those figures current; in return, you decide exactly what the estimate uses.

ClearTill's output is an estimate based on your entries, not financial advice or a guarantee. Read why the product is manual by design:

media.altText: Person using a manually controlled money-planning interface based on a balance, next income date and upcoming costs, with no bank connection.

facebook.text:
Would you rather enter a few figures yourself than connect a money app to your bank? ClearTill gives you that option. You control the balance, dates and costs included, and update them when things change.

That manual control involves effort, and the result depends on what you enter. No bank connection is required. Read the guide:

media.altText: Person reviewing three manually entered planning inputs—balance, next income date and upcoming costs—without connecting a bank account.

instagram.text:
NO BANK CONNECTION
You choose the figures.
You update them.
You can see what the estimate uses.

Manual entry takes effort. For some people, that control is the point. ClearTill estimates from what you enter.

Read the guide via the profile link.

#manualbydesign #privacyconscious #cashposition #cleartill
